### AlphaCFG: Grammar-Guided MCTS for Alpha Generation (arXiv:2601.22119, Jan 2026)
- **Paper**: 'Alpha Discovery via Grammar-Guided Learning and Search' — Yang, Hao, Wang, Shi, Li. Jan 2026. GitHub: https://github.com/HanYang544/AlphaCFG (26 stars, Python 3.9+, Apache 2.0).
- **Method**: Context-free grammar (CFG) constrains factor formula space to syntactically valid expressions. Monte Carlo Tree Search explores grammar-constrained expression trees. Avoids algebraically degenerate factors by construction (grammar rules enforce operator/operand compatibility).
- **S&P 500 results (OOS)**: IC 0.04573 (±0.0034), Sharpe 0.8473 (±0.0483), ICIR 0.4099 (±0.0230). Outperforms AlphaGen/RPN+PPO (IC 0.0342), gplearn (0.0322). NO LLM required — pure symbolic search.
- **Data**: OHLCV + VWAP only (same as QuantaAlpha). Default pipeline uses Baostock (China); Qlib supported as alternative.
- **Comparison to QuantaAlpha**: IC 0.046 vs 0.125-0.150 for Claude-backbone QuantaAlpha. AlphaCFG is significantly weaker on IC but uses fundamentally different generation mechanism (grammar-constrained MCTS vs evolutionary trajectory). Different structural approach = complementary pool diversity.
- **R33 role**: Optional TERTIARY generator. Priority: (1) QuantaAlpha (public code, highest IC, evolutionary trajectory), (2) AlphaPROBE (DAG-aware, complementary lineage tracking), (3) AlphaCFG (grammar-constrained, no LLM cost, structural diversity). Run AlphaCFG only if QuantaAlpha+AlphaPROBE pool has < 20 diverse factors after diversity filter.
- **Implementation**: Python 3.9-3.10, pip install -r requirements.txt, then python run_pool.py. US data: build yfinance HDF5 per Qlib format (same pipeline as QuantaAlpha R33 design).
- **SOURCE**: arXiv:2601.22119
